title: Why Use Tributary?
description: Read [Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/) topics directly from DuckDB SQL. No separate consumer process, no JSON-dump file in the middle — point a `SELECT` at a topic and treat its messages as rows you can `WHERE`, `JOIN`, and `CREATE TABLE AS`.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Tributary makes Kafka topics queryable from inside DuckDB. The path between "messages on a broker" and "rows in a SQL query" collapses to one statement — no consumer code, no intermediate file, no DataFrame round-trip.

bulletPoints.label: Snapshot a topic
bulletPoints.description: Wrap [`tributary_scan_topic`](#tributary_scan_topic) in a [`CREATE TABLE AS`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/create_table) to materialize a topic's current contents for offline analysis.

bulletPoints.label: Join Kafka with local data
bulletPoints.description: Run a `JOIN` between [`tributary_scan_topic`](#tributary_scan_topic) output and a local DuckDB table — the typical pattern for enriching events with reference data on the fly.

bulletPoints.label: Inspect a cluster
bulletPoints.description: [`tributary_metadata`](#tributary_metadata) returns broker and topic descriptors as a row, useful for scripted audits and partition-parallel scan planning.

bulletPoints.label: Ad-hoc analytics
bulletPoints.description: Count, group, window, or aggregate the messages currently on a topic — without building a Kafka Streams or Flink job for a one-off question.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: Internally, Tributary is a thin DuckDB-table-function wrapper around [librdkafka](https://github.com/confluentinc/librdkafka). Every named parameter you pass to a function is forwarded as a librdkafka configuration key, so any consumer-side option Kafka supports is also a Tributary option — broker discovery, SASL, SSL, offset reset, fetch tuning, you name it.

bulletPoints.label: Configuration is parameter-passthrough
bulletPoints.description: Tributary doesn't define its own auth or transport settings. It accepts every name listed in [librdkafka's CONFIGURATION reference](https://github.com/confluentinc/librdkafka/blob/master/CONFIGURATION.md) — `bootstrap.servers`, `group.id`, `security.protocol`, `sasl.*`, `ssl.*`, `auto.offset.reset`, etc. — as a named SQL parameter.

bulletPoints.label: Multi-partition parallelism
bulletPoints.description: [`tributary_scan_topic`](#tributary_scan_topic) reads each partition concurrently, so cluster scans scale with topic partition count rather than serializing through one consumer.

bulletPoints.label: Output shape
bulletPoints.description: Each row from [`tributary_scan_topic`](#tributary_scan_topic) is `(topic, partition, offset, message)`. The message is a `BLOB` — decode it in SQL with DuckDB's [JSON functions](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/loading_json.html), Avro/Protobuf extensions, or `decode(...)` based on your topic's serialization.

bulletPoints.label: No catalog, no secrets
bulletPoints.description: There is no `ATTACH ... (TYPE tributary)` and no managed `CREATE SECRET TYPE tributary`. Every call passes its own credentials through named parameters — for production, source them from `getenv()` and pass via SQL variables so they never appear inline in queries.

sections.title: Production caveats
sections.description: What to know before pointing this at a busy production cluster.

bulletPoints.label: Reads, not writes
bulletPoints.description: The verifiable function surface is consumer-side. There is no documented producer / write-back function in the current version — for cache-priming or topic-publishing workflows, keep a real Kafka producer.

bulletPoints.label: Whole-topic scan by default
bulletPoints.description: [`tributary_scan_topic`](#tributary_scan_topic) reads the topic's current contents. Pair with `WHERE` on `partition` / `offset` / decoded `timestamp`, or use `librdkafka` offset-control parameters (e.g. `auto.offset.reset := 'latest'`) to scope the scan.

bulletPoints.label: Credentials in named parameters
bulletPoints.description: Pass [SASL](https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/#security_sasl) / [SSL](https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/#security_ssl) credentials as `:bind_var` references seeded from `getenv()` — inline literals appear in cached SQL plans.

bulletPoints.label: Experimental status
bulletPoints.description: The function surface may change as more `librdkafka` paths get exposed. Pin a known-good extension version in production CTAS jobs that schedule against this.

useCases.title: Snapshot a topic for offline analysis
useCases.description: [`CREATE TABLE AS SELECT`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/create_table) wrapping [`tributary_scan_topic`](#tributary_scan_topic) — the simplest path from "the events currently on `orders`" to a Parquet-exportable DuckDB table.

useCases.title: Enrich Kafka events with local reference data
useCases.description: Decode JSON messages on the way in, then JOIN against local lookup tables — `users`, `products`, geography. Ideal for audits, sampling, and one-off correlation questions.

useCases.title: Cluster discovery and audit
useCases.description: Use [`tributary_metadata`](#tributary_metadata) to list topics and partition layouts as rows you can `WHERE`/`GROUP BY` — easier than parsing `kafka-topics.sh` output by hand.
